report: Checked all four candidate lemmas end to end. וְ: every difference is the ASV's own connective (Then/and/then/Or/And) read off the text under rule 14, and the one unrepresented waw (25.5 וְלֹא) is an apodosis waw the ASV opens bare. הוּא: his/him are ordinary suffix realizations. לֹא: the *no* of 25.5 is the verbal negation recast as a determiner on the supplied complement *brightness* (rule 15), the two *not*s are plain; no split. עִם: *are with* in 25.2 is a verbless clause whose prepositional phrase is the predicate (rule 49); *with* in 25.4 stands under a finite verb. None of the four is a construction analysed two ways.

Read the dump for added units the lemma table cannot see. The two `added` *that*s of 25.6 stand over noun-plus-noun verbless predications the Hebrew juxtaposes (rule 55); the *he that is* of 25.4 is a supplied noun phrase on an anarthrous substantival participle (rule 46). Different constructions, so no hidden split. The *He* of 25.2 joins the subjectless participle the ASV renders as a finite verb; the competing `added` reading is named in the unit note and the rest of the chapter has no comparable clause, so nothing is inconsistent.

BSB disagreement at 25.5 (וְ of וְלֹא יַאֲהִיל): BSB folds the apodosis waw into its clause; the ASV writes *Behold even the moon hath no brightness* with no connective, and the *even* answers to עַד, which is where it stands. Convention difference, not an error.

No chapter-wide judgment to log and nothing general enough to promote; the participle-with-supplied-subject question at 25.2 rests on one occurrence and rule 17 already covers participles rendered as finite verbs by example.
